recent_articles.title: Unity in diversity: On the INDIA bloc meeting - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Twenty-three Opposition parties**, including the **Congress**, **Samajwadi Party**, and **Trinamool Congress**, met in New Delhi on Monday to address concerns about economic distress, inflation, and educational chaos.  The bloc resolved to write to the Chief Justice of India over electoral fraud allegations, demand the resignation of the Union Education Minister, call for an all-party meeting to discuss the economic crisis, agree to hold coordination meetings every two months, and commit to daily parliamentary coordination during sessions. The meeting followed recent fissures within the alliance, including the absence of the **DMK** and the **Aam Aadmi Party**, highlighting the fragility of the coalition.  Despite these challenges, there is a broad consensus on the need to checkmate the **BJP** for political survival and the health of Indian democracy.

recent_articles.title: Unity in diversity: On the INDIA bloc meeting - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Twenty-three Opposition parties**, including **Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge** and **Leader of the Opposition (Lok Sabha) Rahul Gandhi**, met in Delhi on Monday to address concerns about economic distress, inflation, and educational chaos. The bloc resolved to write to the Chief Justice of India regarding electoral fraud, demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, call for an all-party meeting to address the economic crisis, agree to hold coordination meetings every two months, and commit to daily parliamentary coordination.  The meeting aimed to strengthen institutional framework for Opposition coordination and press the ruling **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** on governance failures.

recent_articles.title: INDIA Bloc Meet Tomorrow, Mamata Banerjee Eyes Help From Frenemy Congress
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leader Jairam Ramesh announced that 23 political parties will participate in the INDIA bloc's meeting tomorrow, with some parties declining attendance due to their own reasons. **DMK** and **AAP**, led by MK Stalin and Arvind Kejriwal respectively, are not attending due to political differences and recent alliance changes.  The meeting is being held at the Constitution Club in Delhi at the behest of **Trinamool Congress** leader Mamata Banerjee who needs support from the bloc to fight the BJP in Bengal.

recent_articles.title: "Party Bigger Than Positions": Karnataka Congress Chief B.K. Hariprasad Amid Cabinet Buzz
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **B.K. Hariprasad**, newly appointed **KPCC** president, emphasized the importance of prioritizing party strength and democratic values over power in leading the Karnataka Congress. He acknowledged concerns about women's representation in the cabinet and assured that it would be addressed during the next expansion.  He also stressed the need to strengthen the party's commitment to inclusivity and social balance, contrasting it with the BJP's single-leader ideology. **Hariprasad** expressed confidence in **D.K. Shivakumar**, the new chief minister, stating that he is capable of leading effectively despite challenges.

recent_articles.title: DK Shivakumar Comes With Mastery Of Delhi Networks And Karnataka Grassroots
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DK Shivakumar**, a seasoned politician, has been appointed the Chief Minister of Karnataka.  He has consistently demonstrated his political acumen and organizational skills throughout his career, navigating complex power dynamics within the Congress party. **Shivakumar**'s ascent to the top position is attributed to his mastery of grassroots electoral math in his home constituency and his ability to build strong networks in Delhi's high-power circles. He skillfully managed a smooth transition of power with **Siddaramaiah**, ensuring a peaceful handover despite persistent speculation about his own ambition for the Chief Minister's role.

recent_articles.title: How the D-day unfolded for DKS, reaching across political divide - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the newly sworn-in Chief Minister of Karnataka, began his day with personal and political gestures, including calls to MLAs and a visit to former Chief Ministers **B.S. Yediyurappa** and **H.D. Deve Gowda**. He chose traditional attire for his oath ceremony and invited Congress leaders **Rahul Gandhi**, **Mallikarjun Kharge**, and **Sonia Gandhi** to the event, which was attended by high-ranking members of the **Congress** party from other states.  The ceremony also included a gathering of religious leaders representing various faiths.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar Takes Oath, G Parameshwara Is His Deputy
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DK Shivakumar**, a prominent figure in the **Congress**, took oath as the Chief Minister of Karnataka, ending a two-year political tussle. His cabinet of 13 ministers includes his predecessor's son, **Yathindra Siddaramaiah**.  G Parameshwara was appointed Deputy Chief Minister, balancing social factions within the party. The event saw participation from Congress leaders like **Rahul Gandhi**, **Priyanka Gandhi Vadra**, and other state chief ministers. Shivakumar expressed gratitude to the **Gandhi family** for their support in his political journey.

recent_articles.title: dk shivakumar oath ceremony live updates karnataka chief minister cabinet ministers swearing in siddaramaiah yathindra siddaramaiah congress rahul gandhi sonia gandhi
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DK Shivakumar** will be sworn in as the chief minister of Karnataka today at 4 pm.  The ceremony, to be held at the Glass House in Lok Bhavan, will see the swearing-in of ten ministers, including **Yathindra Siddaramaiah**, son of former Chief Minister **Siddaramaiah**.  **Rahul Gandhi** and **Mallikarjun Kharge** are expected to attend. **Sonia Gandhi** congratulated **Shivakumar** on Wednesday.

recent_articles.title: DK Shivakumar career: From student leader to Karnataka CM frontrunner - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DK Shivakumar**, a former student leader, has consistently risen through the ranks of the **Congress** party in Karnataka over four decades.  He won eight Assembly elections, securing a commanding 75% vote share in 2023. His rise to prominence began in 1981 when he joined the National Students' Union of India and later served as chairman of the Karnataka State Planning Board. **Shivakumar** also played a key role in organizing the historic campaign yatra that brought SM Krishna's Congress to power, defeating HD Kumaraswamy in Sathanur in 1999. He has held various ministerial positions and led the Congress party's 2023 Karnataka campaign, ultimately becoming deputy chief minister after winning his own seat with a strong majority.

recent_articles.title: Rahul Gandhi as PM | Modi’s enablers - The Gandhi family and the BJP’s dominance - Telegraph India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A recent article criticizes the leadership of **Rahul Gandhi** and his sister, **Priyanka Gandhi**, within the **Congress Party**.  The author argues that despite the party's gains in the 2024 general elections, their lack of discipline, gravitas, and a clear vision for governance have hindered their progress. The author suggests that the Congress has lost ground to the **Bharatiya Janata Party** in many states, while highlighting the need for a new leader who can inspire voters and address the public's concerns about economic mismanagement and rising inequality.  The article also criticizes the reliance on dynastic politics within the party, comparing it to similar situations in other countries like Hungary where a fresh face emerged as an effective opposition leader.

recent_articles.title: Congress move to bring Girish Chodankar back to helm Goa unit sparks discontent | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** appointed **Girish Chodankar** as the new Goa Pradesh Congress Committee (GPCC) president, replacing **Amit Patkar**. This move has sparked discontent among some party leaders who question Chodankar's 2022 performance in Goa and his appointment after a three-year absence from the post.  **Patkar**, who skipped the event where Chodankar took charge, is reportedly planning to form a new political party with his supporters. The **AICC** has also appointed three new state working presidents: **M K Shaikh**, **Altone D’Costa**, and **Carlos Alvares Ferreira**.

recent_articles.title: Stage set for DK Shivakumar’s swearing-in as CM on June 3; government, party rejigs on cards | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D K Shivakumar**, the newly elected leader of the **Karnataka Congress Legislature Party (CLP)**, will be sworn in as Chief Minister on June 3rd.  The CLP unanimously chose him following the resignation of **Siddaramaiah**, who stepped down to make way for a power-sharing agreement with Shivakumar. The new CM is expected to appoint a new Cabinet and may include several new faces while dropping over half of the ministers from the previous government. **K C Venugopal** and **Randeep Surjewala**, both AICC officials, were present at the CLP meeting and confirmed the transition.  The Governor has invited Shivakumar to take oath along with his new ministers.

recent_articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar meets Governor Gehlot, stakes claim to form new govt in Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the newly elected leader of the **Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee**, will be sworn in as Chief Minister on Wednesday, June 3rd at Lok Bhavan. The event is expected to be attended by the central leadership of the party and Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot has invited him to take the oath at 4:05 p.m.  The power transition was overseen by **Mallikarjun Kharge**, **Rahul Gandhi**, and **Sonia Gandhi**.  With Cabinet formation still under discussion, speculation remains about whether a full Cabinet will be sworn in and if there will be deputy Chief Ministers.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka government formation LIVE: Congress to convene crucial CLP meeting at 4 p.m. on May 30 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, after resigning as the chief minister of Karnataka, met with **Rahul Gandhi** at **Sonia Gandhi’s** residence. The meeting focused on his future role within the **Congress** party and included discussions about his son's potential positions in the new government.  **Siddaramaiah** also met with **Mallikarjun Kharge**, the Congress chief, to discuss the transition process.

recent_articles.title: AICC begins consultations with Kerala leaders in New Delhi to decide on Congress’ CM candidate - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, **Sonia Gandhi**, and **Mallikarjun Kharge** met with top Kerala leaders in New Delhi on Tuesday to discuss the selection of a Chief Minister nominee for the state. The high command is seeking bipartisan support from former KPCC presidents, Congress MLAs-elect, and other key figures to restore organizational stability after the party's recent victory.  The meeting considered several potential candidates, including **K.C. Venugopal**, **V.D. Satheesan**, **Ramesh Chennithala**, and **Priyanka Gandhi Vadra**.  **K. Muraleedharan**, a KPCC insider, stated that the high command would consider popular opinion in addition to legislative party numbers when making their decision.

recent_articles.title: Bail order reminder that personal liberty can’t be sacrificed for political vendetta: Pawan Khera - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pawan Khera**, a Congress leader, was granted anticipatory bail by the **Supreme Court** after allegations were made against him regarding his comments on Assam Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma's** wife. The court found that the matter appeared to stem from political rivalry and granted pre-arrest bail with certain conditions.  **Abhishek Singhvi**, along with other legal representatives, defended Khera's liberty amidst threats and intimidation. The Congress hailed the decision as a victory for the rule of law, urging **Sarma** to reconsider his language and apologize.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court takes suo motu note of assault on woman advocate, issues directions - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** took suo motu action in a brutal assault case involving a woman advocate in New Delhi, directing the Delhi Police Commissioner to hand over the investigation to a senior officer. The court also ordered the police to look into three hospitals' refusal of admission to the victim and investigate allegations against her husband's in-laws regarding the disappearance of her two minor children. **Manoj Kumar**, the alleged assailant, was arrested on April 26th after confessing to stabbing his wife on April 22nd during a family dispute.

recent_articles.title: A season to try and understand the people’s pulse - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sonia Gandhi** made her debut election speech in Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu on January 11, 1998, amidst a backdrop of political tension and the legacy of Rajiv Gandhi's assassination.  During the campaign, voters expressed their support for **Congress** through slogans like "Zindabad," while others displayed strong emotional ties to parties like the **AIADMK**, exemplified by an elderly woman who identified with the party's symbol despite its opposition.

recent_articles.title: AIADMK looks to defend Melur and Usilampatti, its southern strongholds - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Despite internal conflicts within the AIADMK, the party appears to be favored in Melur and Usilampatti constituencies.  Incumbent MLA Periyapullan (AIADMK) faces a challenge from former Congress MP P. Viswanathan in Melur, where caste consciousness is prominent. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and the Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are expected to impact the outcome. In Usilampatti, I. Mahendran (AIADMK) faces off against P. Ayyappan (AIPTMMK) and T. Saravanakumar (Congress).  The election is likely to be influenced by caste dynamics and local political alliances.

recent_articles.title: National Herald case: Delhi High Court to hear on Monday ED plea against Sonia, Rahul - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Delhi High Court** will hear a case on Monday, April 20, 2026, where the **Enforcement Directorate (ED)** challenges a trial court's refusal to take cognisance of its charge sheet against **Sonia Gandhi**, **Rahul Gandhi**, and others in the National Herald-linked money laundering case. The ED alleges that these individuals conspired and laundered funds through Young Indian, a company they controlled, allegedly acquiring properties worth ₹2,000 crore from Associated Journals Limited (AJL), publisher of the National Herald newspaper.  The trial court's order stated that the agency's probe stemmed from a private complaint and not an FIR, arguing that cognisance cannot be taken on such complaints. The ED argues that this decision is flawed and undermines its efforts to prosecute money laundering cases.

recent_articles.title: Vem Narender Reddy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Vem Narender Reddy** and **Abhishek Manu Singhvi**, both from Telangana, were sworn in as Rajya Sabha MPs on Thursday.  After the oath-taking ceremony, **Reddy** met with **Sonia Gandhi** to express his gratitude for her selection.

recent_articles.title: T.N. Assembly election: Jayalalithaa would have opposed delimitation if she were alive, says Stalin - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **M.K. Stalin**, DMK president, criticized the **AIADMK** for its lack of opposition to delimitation and accused the BJP of attempting to suppress the voice of southern states. He argued that the BJP's focus on delimitation during elections is a ploy to divert attention from pressing issues like gas cylinder shortages. **Stalin** compared the BJP's actions to the making of makkan beda, highlighting the deceptive nature of their intentions. He emphasized that Tamil Nadu should resist attempts by Delhi to control its political future and protect its rights.

recent_articles.title: Congress issues three-line whip to its Lok Sabha MPs; unlikely to back delimitation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** issued a three-line whip to its Lok Sabha members urging them to support the party's stance during the upcoming special session of Parliament, which will focus on amending the women’s reservation law and carrying out a delimitation exercise. The government plans to increase the strength of both the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies by 50%, reserving 272 seats for women lawmakers. **Congress** president Mallikarjun Kharge and party chairperson Sonia Gandhi have expressed concerns about the timing of the special session, arguing that it is being held in the middle of an election campaign and that delimitation should be addressed separately.

recent_articles.title: Revanth sees ‘political motive’ in linking Women’s Bill with delimitation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Revanth Reddy** accused the **Union Government** of misleadingly linking the Women’s Reservation Bill with constituency delimitation to create a narrative that opposition parties are obstructing reforms. He argued that these issues should be discussed and implemented independently, highlighting the Congress party's long history of supporting women's empowerment.  He criticized the BJP for its lack of support for the bill and pointed out the absence of female leadership within the party since its inception in 1980.

recent_articles.title: Congress discusses women’s reservation law and delimitation; Kharge to meet other Opposition leaders for joint strategy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Congress Working Committee** (CWC) discussed the government's proposed delimitation exercise and women's reservation law implementation. The party plans to formulate a joint strategy for the upcoming special session of Parliament, aiming to implement the women's reservation law by 2029 and increase the strength of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies by 50%.  **Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge**, **Sonia Gandhi**, and **Rahul Gandhi** expressed concerns about the proposed changes, emphasizing the need for wider consultation on delimitation. The party also criticized the government's move to implement a predetermined number of seats for women, arguing that it undermines proportional representation for other marginalized groups.

recent_articles.title: Sharan Prakash Patil takes umbrage at remarks by BJP leaders against Mallikarjun Kharge - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr. Sharan Prakash Patil**, **Medical Education Minister**, criticized **BJP leaders** for making "irresponsible" and "disrespectful" remarks against **AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge**.  Patil condemned the comments, arguing that they are being blown out of proportion and comparing them to past instances of similar attacks by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on Congress leaders. He also questioned the basis for comparisons made by **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** against **Jawaharlal Nehru**, emphasizing the Congress's commitment to non-alignment and condemnation of aggression without supporting war.

recent_articles.title: Mallikarjun Kharge expresses regret over 'illiterate' remark, says he has highest of respect for Gujaratis - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge** issued a statement expressing regret for his controversial remarks about the people of Gujarat during an election speech in Kerala. He clarified that he never intended to offend the people of Gujarat and maintains respect for them. The **BJP** demanded an apology from **Kharge**, accusing him of making "shameless, demeaning and utterly despicable" statements.

recent_articles.title: Once BJP comes to power in West Bengal, all infiltrators will be sent back: Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, asserted that a change is inevitable in West Bengal and that all infiltrators from Assam, Tripura, and Bengal will be sent back to their countries if the BJP comes to power. He accused the **Congress** of supporting illegal immigrants and claimed that the party opposes the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) because it knows the law will prevent infiltrators from remaining in the state.  He also criticized the **Congress**, accusing them of building madrasas for Muslim students and calling the RSS and BJP snakes.

recent_articles.title: Kerala election 2026: Polls heat up as major fronts step up campaigns and identity politics takes centrestage - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: With the Kerala Assembly polls approaching, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Rahul Gandhi**, and **Priyanka Gandhi Vadra** are among the high-profile figures campaigning. The election has become increasingly polarized with accusations of backroom deals and communal overtures from groups like the SDPI and JIH.  The ruling **CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front (LDF)** is highlighting a decade of development, while the **United Democratic Front (UDF)** faces internal strife over its leadership and attempts to revive the Sabarimala gold theft scandal. The BJP seeks to expand its vote share into actual seats, but faces challenges from the FCRA issue with the Christian electorate.

recent_articles.title: ‘Regional imbalance’ bothers Congress as government plans delimitation to roll out women’s reservation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union government** has proposed to implement the women's reservation law by 2029 using the 2011 Census data, reversing its previous stance. This proposal has prompted the **Congress** to call for an all-party meeting to discuss potential implications of such a move. The Congress argues that a uniform 50% increase in seats could widen the representation gap between states with larger populations and those with smaller populations.  The party is also seeking clarity on how the government plans to address demands for representation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes within the women's reservation framework.

recent_articles.title: NDA, Opposition spar in LS over efforts to free country of Maoism - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** and **NDA** members in the Lok Sabha criticized the previous **UPA** government for its handling of Maoism, accusing it of failing to contain the threat.  They highlighted significant reductions in the "red corridor" under the current administration and emphasized the success of policies like Operation Green Hunt and the creation of CoBRA. The Congress countered by pointing to efforts made during their tenure, including the establishment of the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA) and emphasizing a balanced approach that prioritized both security and welfare.  The debate highlighted contrasting approaches to combating Maoism between the two governments.

recent_articles.title: Sonia Gandhi shows 'excellent progress', discharge expected soon, say doctors - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sonia Gandhi**, a senior Congress leader, has made excellent progress and is now "absolutely normal" after being admitted to **Sir Ganga Ram Hospital** on March 24th with a fever. Doctors confirmed that she remains on IV antibiotics for the next few days but all her parameters are within normal limits. A decision regarding her discharge will be made jointly by doctors and the patient, who is currently stable and under observation briefly as a precaution.

recent_articles.title: CPI(M)’s criticism of Rahul Gandhi to please BJP: Sachin Pilot - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sachin Pilot**, general secretary of the **All India Congress Committee**, accused **Pinarayi Vijayan**, chief minister of Kerala, and the **CPI(M)** of making allegations against **Rahul Gandhi** to appease the **BJP**.  Pilot alleged that these accusations are part of a deal between the two parties. He also criticized the LDF government's handling of issues like cooking gas shortages and economic development in the state.

recent_articles.title: Govt revs up consultations on early implementation of Women’s Reservation Act - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Narendra Modi** government announced plans to amend the Women’s Reservation Act, 2023 to implement its provisions for the 2029 Lok Sabha election. The amendment will reserve one-third of seats in Parliament and State Assemblies for women based on the 2011 Census data.  The **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** met with leaders from various Opposition parties including the Nationalist Congress Party, YSR Congress Party, All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen, and Shiv Sena (UBT) to discuss the proposed amendments. The government aims to introduce these amendments in Parliament during the ongoing Budget Session or a Special Session later this year.

recent_articles.title: Revanth Reddy is building his own band of loyalists - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Revanth Reddy**, the Chief Minister of Telangana, is consolidating his power within both the government and the state Congress party. He has appointed several young, recently joined Congress members to key positions, including Assembly and Legislative Council Whips.  This move signals a clear intention to shape the party's future leadership with his own loyalists. While a coordination committee was formed to bridge the gap between the government and the party, **Revanth Reddy**’s recent actions suggest he is determined to maintain control within the party structure.

recent_articles.title: Deve Gowda writes to Sonia Gandhi over ‘chaos’ in Parliament - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **H.D. Deve Gowda**, former Prime Minister and leader of the Janata Dal (Secular), expressed concern over "chaos" in Parliament during the ongoing Budget Session, particularly regarding disruptions by the **Congress Parliamentary Party**.  He urged **Sonia Gandhi**, chairperson of the **Congress Parliamentary Party**, to intervene and restore parliamentary traditions and decorum. Gowda emphasized that protests should be conducted through established methods and not disrupt proceedings or create an atmosphere of disrespect for the institution.
